4. Pairwise contrasts and multiple comparisons

Source: vignettes/4-contrasts.Rmd
4-contrasts.Rmd

comparison methods

When comparing specific groups there are two reasonable questions, and permanova_contrasts() lets you choose which one you’re asking with the method argument.

method = "isolated" (the default) asks: “Do these two groups differ, considering just those two groups?” It pulls out only the samples from the levels being compared and runs a fresh two-group PERMANOVA on them — its own error term, its own permutations (the approach that PRIMER takes for pairwise comparisons). It makes no assumptions about the other groups in your design.

A third question — “do they differ within each level of something else?” — is answered by within =, covered in section vii.

method = "pooled" asks: “Do these two groups differ, using the error estimated from the whole experiment?” It tests the same difference but borrows the error term from the full model, which uses all your data and so can have more power. The trade-off is that it assumes the groups are similarly variable (homogeneous dispersion) — if one group is much more scattered than another, this assumption is questionable.

Use isolated when you want a clean, assumption-light comparison that matches PRIMER (i.e. default). Use pooled when your groups are similarly variable and you want the extra power from the shared error term.

pairwise and multicomparisons:

i) one-way pairwise contrasts:

Using the dune data: which management regimes differ in dune plant composition?

all pairwise comparisons among the four management levels (6 contrasts), Holm-adjusted:


data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")
bray <- vegdist(dune, method = "bray")

fit1 <- permanova(bray ~ Management, data = dune.env,
                  permutations = 9999, seed = 101)
summary(fit1)
#> Distance-based PERMANOVA
#> Engine: fixed effects  (Type I SS)
#> 
#> Factors
#>  Name       Type  Levels
#>  Management Fixed 4     
#> 
#> PERMANOVA table of results
#>  Source     df SS    MS    Pseudo-F P(perm) P(MC)  Unique perms
#>  Management 3  1.469 0.490 2.7672   0.0027  0.0054 9999        
#>  Residual   16 2.830 0.177                                     
#>  Total      19 4.299                                           
#> 
#> Details of the expected mean squares (EMS) for the model
#>  Source     EMS                           
#>  Management 1*V(Res) + 4.900*S(Management)
#>  Res        1*V(Res)                      
#> 
#> Construction of Pseudo-F ratio(s) from mean squares
#>  Source     Numerator    Denominator Num.df Den.df
#>  Management 1*Management 1*Res       3      16    
#> 
#> Estimates of components of variation
#>  Source        Estimate Sq.root
#>  S(Management) 0.064    0.253  
#>  V(Res)        0.177    0.421

permanova_contrasts(fit1, type = "pairwise") |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
BF - HF 1.568 1 6 MS[full-model Residual] 0.200 9999 TRUE 0.241
BF - NM 2.715 1 7 MS[full-model Residual] 0.022 9999 TRUE 0.112
BF - SF 2.515 1 7 MS[full-model Residual] 0.059 9999 TRUE 0.178
HF - NM 3.423 1 9 MS[full-model Residual] 0.029 9999 TRUE 0.116
HF - SF 1.857 1 9 MS[full-model Residual] 0.121 9999 TRUE 0.241
NM - SF 3.426 1 10 MS[full-model Residual] 0.005 9999 TRUE 0.031

same, but control the family-wise error differently (Benjamini-Hochberg):

permanova_contrasts(fit1, type = "pairwise", adjust = "BH")  |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
BF - HF 1.568 1 6 MS[full-model Residual] 0.200 9999 TRUE 0.200
BF - NM 2.715 1 7 MS[full-model Residual] 0.022 9999 TRUE 0.058
BF - SF 2.515 1 7 MS[full-model Residual] 0.059 9999 TRUE 0.089
HF - NM 3.423 1 9 MS[full-model Residual] 0.029 9999 TRUE 0.058
HF - SF 1.857 1 9 MS[full-model Residual] 0.121 9999 TRUE 0.145
NM - SF 3.426 1 10 MS[full-model Residual] 0.005 9999 TRUE 0.031

ii) treatment vs control:

Using the pyrifos dataset (12 ditches, 11 weeks, dose applied per ditch): does each pesticide dose differ from the untreated control?

every dose vs control (dose = 0): 4 contrasts:

data(pyrifos, package = "vegan")
ditch <- gl(12, 1, length = 132)
week  <- gl(11, 12, labels = c(-4, -1, 0.1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 15, 19, 24))
dose  <- factor(rep(c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6), 11))
pyr.env  <- data.frame(ditch, week, dose)
pyr.bray <- vegdist(pyrifos)

fit2 <- permanova(pyr.bray ~ dose, data = pyr.env,
                  permutations = 999, seed = 101)


permanova_contrasts(fit2, type = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "0") |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
0.1 - 0 2.313 1 64 MS[full-model Residual] 0.007 999 TRUE 0.007
0.9 - 0 3.963 1 64 MS[full-model Residual] 0.002 999 TRUE 0.004
6 - 0 6.224 1 64 MS[full-model Residual] 0.001 999 TRUE 0.004
44 - 0 10.726 1 64 MS[full-model Residual] 0.001 999 TRUE 0.004

iii) polynomial contrasts

is there a monotone (linear) compositional trend across dose, and any curvature?


permanova_contrasts(fit2, type = "poly", scores = c(0, 0.1, 0.9, 6, 44))  |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
linear 10.781 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
quadratic 5.018 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
cubic 3.666 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
quartic 2.854 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA

if dose were an ordered factor with numeric labels, scores are inferred:

pyr.env$dose_ord <- ordered(pyr.env$dose,
                            levels = c("0", "0.1", "0.9", "6", "44"))
fit2b <- permanova(pyr.bray ~ dose_ord, data = pyr.env,
                   permutations = 999, seed = 101)
permanova_contrasts(fit2b, type = "poly")    |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
linear 10.781 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
quadratic 5.018 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
cubic 3.666 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
quartic 2.854 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA

iii) sum to zero (grand mean) 


permanova_contrasts(fit1, type = "contr.sum") |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
BF - mean 2.515 1 7 MS[full-model Residual] 0.059 9999 TRUE 0.119
HF - mean 1.857 1 9 MS[full-model Residual] 0.121 9999 TRUE 0.121
NM - mean 3.426 1 10 MS[full-model Residual] 0.005 9999 TRUE 0.016

iv) helmert contrasts

helmert (i.e. each level vs the mean of subsequent levels):


permanova_contrasts(fit1, type = "helmert") |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
helmert_1 1.568 1 6 MS[full-model Residual] 0.2 9999 TRUE 0.2
helmert_2 4.761 1 16 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
helmert_3 2.829 1 16 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA

v) custom contrasts

Test a specific ecological hypothesis: do the low doses (0, 0.1, 0.9) together differ from the high doses (6, 44)? Columns MUST be in the factor’s level order; check with levels():


Lm <- rbind(
  "low vs high"   = c( 1/3,  1/3,  1/3, -1/2, -1/2),    # note level order!
  "44 vs 6"       = c(   0,    0,    0,    1,   -1)
)
permanova_contrasts(fit2, type = "custom", custom = Lm) |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
low vs high 11.754 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
44 vs 6 2.536 1 42 MS[full-model Residual] 0.008 999 TRUE 0.008

a named list works too, one vector per contrast:


Llist <- list(
  "any dose vs control" = c(-4, 1, 1, 1, 1),            # control vs the rest
  "top dose vs control" = c(-1, 0, 0, 1, 0)             # 44 vs 0
)
permanova_contrasts(fit2, type = "custom", custom = Llist) |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
any dose vs control 7.097 1 127 Residual (pooled; isolated undefined for >2-level contrast) NA NA TRUE NA
top dose vs control 6.224 1 64 MS[full-model Residual] 0.001 999 TRUE 0.001

vi) contrasts with random effects:

does treatment differ, tested at the correct level, with repeated samples per site?


set.seed(7)
site  <- factor(rep(paste0("S", 1:8), each = 4))
treat <- factor(rep(c("ctrl", "trt"), each = 16))   # S1-S4 ctrl, S5-S8 trt
comm  <- matrix(rpois(32 * 15, 5), 32, 15)
d     <- vegdist(comm)
env   <- data.frame(site, treat)

fit3 <- permanova(d ~ treat + (1 | site), data = env,
                  permutations = 999, seed = 202)


permanova_contrasts(fit3, type = "pairwise") |> tab()
contrast pseudo_F df_num df_den denominator p_perm unique_perms estimable p_adj
ctrl - trt 1.751 1 6 MS[site within fixed model] 0.115 999 TRUE 0.115

vii) contrasts within the cells of other factors

Sometimes the question is not “do these two levels differ?” but “do they differ here” — depths compared separately within each region, treatments within each site. within = names the factors whose combinations define the cells:

set.seed(11)
# north sampled on five sites, south on one
site   <- factor(rep(paste0("S", 1:6), each = 12))
region <- factor(c(rep("north", 60), rep("south", 12)))
depth  <- factor(rep(c("shallow", "mid", "deep"), times = 24),
                 levels = c("shallow", "mid", "deep"))
comm   <- matrix(rpois(72 * 12, 5), 72, 12)
reef   <- data.frame(site, region, depth)

fit4 <- permanova(vegdist(comm) ~ depth * region + (1 | site) + (1 | site:depth),
                  data = reef, permutations = 0, seed = 11)

permanova_contrasts(fit4, type = "pairwise", factor = "depth",
                    within = "region", permutations = 999, seed = 11)
#> Pairwise contrasts of 'depth' within region
#>   6 contrasts in 2 cells; strata rebuilt per pair
#> 
#> north
#>  contrast       t      df denominator  p_perm
#>  shallow - mid  0.7789 4  1*site:depth 0.643 
#>  shallow - deep 1.3816 4  1*site:depth 0.124 
#>  mid - deep     0.7514 4  1*site:depth 0.613 
#> 
#> south
#>  contrast       t      df denominator p_perm
#>  shallow - mid  0.9896 6  1*Residual  0.540 
#>  shallow - deep 0.8105 6  1*Residual  0.794 
#>  mid - deep     1.3242 6  1*Residual  0.114

Naming several factors in factor is shorthand for the same thing — the first is contrasted inside combinations of the rest — and the reading taken is reported:

permanova_contrasts(fit4, type = "pairwise", factor = c("depth", "region"))
#> Contrasting 'depth' within region.

why each pair gets its own denominator

The denominator cannot be inherited from the parent fit, and the output above shows why. In the north, five sites support the site-by-depth stratum, so that is what the depth contrast is tested against. In the south there is one site, that stratum has no degrees of freedom at all, and the contrast falls back to the residual — a different denominator and a different number of degrees of freedom, in the same table.

So each pair rebuilds the declared random strata on its own subset, drops the ones that have collapsed, and matches the contrast’s expected mean square against whichever survive. Three pairs inside one cell can legitimately carry three different denominators, which no single fitted model can produce. The permutation follows the same logic: whole units of the stratum carrying the denominator are exchanged, rather than individual observations, so a cell with forty samples across six units is not treated as forty independent replicates.

This is what PRIMER reports as a “within level” pairwise table, and permanova_contrasts_within() is the same routine if you prefer to call it directly. It is defined for type = "pairwise" only: other families need a contrast matrix over all levels, which a single cell need not carry.

contrast matrix

contrast_matrix() is exported so you can see/verify the L matrix a family produces — useful for checking custom coding or level order before you run thousands of permutations.

contrast_matrix("trt.vs.ctrl", levels = levels(pyr.env$dose), ref = "0")
#>          0 0.1 0.9 6 44
#> 0.1 - 0 -1   1   0 0  0
#> 0.9 - 0 -1   0   1 0  0
#> 6 - 0   -1   0   0 1  0
#> 44 - 0  -1   0   0 0  1
# contrast_matrix("poly", levels = levels(pyr.env$dose),
#                 scores = c(0, 0.1, 0.9, 44, 6))          # matches level order
# contrast_matrix("pairwise", levels = levels(dune.env$Management))

programmatic use 


library(distmer)
library(vegan)

data(pyrifos)

ditch <- gl(12, 1, length = 132)
week  <- gl(11, 12, labels = c(-4, -1, 0.1, 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 15, 19, 24))
dose  <- factor(rep(c(0.1, 0, 0, 0.9, 0, 44, 6, 0.1, 44, 0.9, 0, 6), 11))

pyr.env <- data.frame(ditch, week, dose)
pyr.bray <- vegdist(pyrifos)

fit <- permanova(
  pyr.bray ~ dose,
  data = pyr.env,
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 101
)

res <- permanova_contrasts(fit, type = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "0")
as.data.frame(res) |> tab()                      # full numeric table
summary(res)                             # same data.frame
subset(as.data.frame(res), p_adj < 0.05) # significant contrasts only
res$L

```
